findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — unwrap() on fallible I/O will panic on missing file, permission error, or invalid UTF-8
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed domain error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, E> and propagate errors with ? or explicit Err. Use a domain error type such as IoError or LoadError.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap() on parse failure (invalid digits, empty field) panics
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV input aborts the entire job loading instead of reporting which line and field failed
findings.fix: Return Result and use .map_err() to convert ParseIntError into a domain error (e.g., ParseError). Chain with ? to propagate.

findings.problem: .parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 — lossy as-cast from u32 to u16 silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value such as 70000 becomes 4464 without any error, corrupting the data silently
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) with map_err to return a typed overflow error. Never use as for narrowing casts.

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] — unchecked indexed access into Vec without any bounds check
findings.failure_mode: a line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields panics via index out of bounds, crashing the caller
findings.fix: Use get(0) and get(1) with map_err, or prefer split_once(',') to avoid collecting into Vec and to extract exactly two fields with proper None handling.

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() — collects all split parts into a Vec when only two fields (name, value) are needed
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line, and if a line contains extra commas the extra data is silently discarded, hiding malformed input
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to split into exactly two parts. This avoids the intermediate Vec, the per-line allocation, and the silent data loss on extra fields.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — console-side-effect embedded in data-loading pipeline
findings.failure_mode: hidden I/O side effect pollutes stdout, breaks piping, and couples data-loading logic to console output; makes the function impossible to test deterministically
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely. If logging is needed, pass a logger abstraction or return a separate log/diagnostic collection from the shell layer.

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 — no domain newtypes for name or value
findings.failure_mode: any string and any u16 (including 0, overflowed, or negative) can be constructed, making illegal states representable
findings.fix: Introduce newtype wrappers (e.g., JobName(String), JobValue(u16)) with constructors that enforce invariants such as non-empty name and value > 0.

findings.problem: load_jobs performs file I/O and returns concrete Vec<Record> instead of Result — hidden I/O
findings.failure_mode: callers have no way to handle I/O errors; the function signature lies about not failing, so callers skip error handling and the program crashes on any disk failure
findings.fix: Signature should be fn load_jobs(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>. Pure parsing should be extracted into a separate pure function: fn parse_records(lines: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for allocation behavior or throughput of load_jobs
no profiler evidence for the per-line heap allocation from split().collect()
no allocation audit — each line heap-allocates a Vec<String>, multiple String allocations per line
no command-line interface evidence or integration test coverage for load_jobs
residual_risk: static review only — no commands run. All 8 findings are directly observable in source. The function is entirely broken for any real-world input: panics on missing file, malformed lines, parse errors, and silently truncates u32 values. The architecture mixes I/O and parsing in a single impure function with no error surface. Full rewrite with Result types, split_once, checked conversions, and pure/push separation is required before this crate is acceptable.
